questions.q: Which Gupta ruler was called the 'Napoleon of India' by the historian V.A. Smith?
questions.solution: V.A. Smith called **Samudragupta** the 'Napoleon of India' because of his long run of military campaigns, which are recorded in the Allahabad (Prayag) Pillar inscription.
questions.shortcut: Conqueror + pillar full of victories = Samudragupta.

questions.q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by —
questions.solution: Brothers **Harihara and Bukka** of the Sangama dynasty founded Vijayanagara in 1336. Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva dynasty) was its best-known later ruler; Hasan Bahman Shah founded the rival Bahmani kingdom in 1347.
questions.shortcut: 1336 = Sangama brothers; 1347 = Bahmani.

questions.q: Who founded the Servants of India Society in 1905?
questions.solution: **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** founded the Servants of India Society at Poona in 1905 to train workers for national service. Gokhale was a moderate leader and is regarded as Gandhi's political guru.
questions.shortcut: Gokhale = 'servants' — a moderate's society of trained volunteers.

questions.q: The Rowlatt Act, against which Gandhi launched a nationwide satyagraha, was passed in —
questions.solution: The **Rowlatt Act (March 1919)** allowed detention without trial. Protests against it led up to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 in Amritsar.
questions.shortcut: Rowlatt and Jallianwala Bagh belong to the same year — 1919.

questions.q: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of which state?
questions.solution: **Mohiniyattam**, a graceful solo dance performed by women, belongs to **Kerala**. Kerala's other classical form is Kathakali.
questions.shortcut: Kerala has two classical dances: Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

questions.q: Pandit Ravi Shankar is famous for playing which musical instrument?
questions.solution: **Pandit Ravi Shankar** (Bharat Ratna, 1999) was the sitar player who made Indian classical music known around the world.
questions.shortcut: Ravi Shankar = sitar; Zakir Hussain = tabla; Ram Narayan = sarangi.

questions.q: Yakshagana, a traditional theatre form combining dance, music and dialogue, belongs to which state?
questions.solution: **Yakshagana** is the traditional theatre form of coastal **Karnataka**. Kerala is the usual trap because Yakshagana's costumes look like those of Kathakali.
questions.shortcut: Yakshagana = coastal Karnataka (Udupi and Dakshina Kannada).

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the Finance Commission?
questions.solution: **Article 280** requires the President to set up a Finance Commission every five years to recommend how taxes are shared between the Union and the States.
questions.shortcut: 280 = Finance Commission; 324 = Election Commission; 312 = All India Services.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution: Under Article 84, a person must be at least **25 years** old to become a Lok Sabha member. The Rajya Sabha requires 30, and the President and Vice-President require 35.
questions.shortcut: Lok Sabha 25, Rajya Sabha 30, President 35.

questions.q: The Governor of a state holds office during the pleasure of the —
options: Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.solution: Under Article 156, the Governor holds office **during the pleasure of the President**, who also appoints the Governor (Article 155).
questions.shortcut: The President appoints the Governor and can remove them.

questions.q: The provisions on disqualification on grounds of defection (the anti-defection law) are contained in which Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.solution: The **Tenth Schedule** contains the anti-defection provisions. The Eighth Schedule lists languages, the Ninth protects certain laws from judicial review, and the Seventh contains the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.
questions.shortcut: Defection → Tenth Schedule.

questions.q: Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
questions.solution: The **Godavari** (about 1,465 km) is the longest peninsular river, which is why it is called the 'Dakshin Ganga'. The Krishna comes second.
questions.shortcut: Dakshin Ganga = Godavari = longest in the south.

questions.q: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.solution: **Gujarat** has the longest coastline of any Indian state, including the Gulf of Kachchh and the Gulf of Khambhat. Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu follow.
questions.shortcut: Two gulfs (Kachchh and Khambhat) give Gujarat the longest coast.

questions.q: The Suez Canal connects which two water bodies?
questions.solution: The **Suez Canal** in Egypt connects the **Mediterranean Sea** with the **Red Sea**, so ships can travel between Europe and Asia without going around Africa. The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific.
questions.shortcut: Suez = Mediterranean to Red Sea; Panama = Atlantic to Pacific.

questions.q: Which body regulates the insurance sector in India?
questions.solution: The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** regulates insurance. SEBI regulates securities markets and PFRDA regulates pensions.
questions.shortcut: Insurance → IRDAI; shares → SEBI; pensions → PFRDA.

questions.q: The repo rate is the rate at which —
options: commercial banks lend to their best customers
the RBI borrows money from commercial banks
the government borrows from the public
the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
questions.solution: The **repo rate** is the rate at which the **RBI lends** short-term money to commercial banks against government securities. When the RBI instead absorbs money from banks, that is the reverse-repo idea.
questions.shortcut: Repo = RBI lends to banks. Reverse repo = banks park money with the RBI.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.solution: Resistance is measured in **ohms** (Ω). By Ohm's law, R = V/I. The volt measures potential difference, the ampere measures current, and the watt measures power.
questions.shortcut: R = V / I → volt per ampere = ohm.

questions.q: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.solution: A **convex mirror** always forms an erect, smaller image and shows a **wider field of view**, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror. Concave mirrors are used in headlights and for shaving.
questions.shortcut: Rear-view → wide view → convex.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of washing soda?
questions.solution: Washing soda is **sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na2CO3·10H2O**. NaHCO3 is baking soda, CaOCl2 is bleaching powder, and CaSO4·½H2O is plaster of Paris.
questions.shortcut: Washing soda has 10 waters of crystallisation.

questions.q: Vegetable oils are converted into vanaspati ghee by passing which gas through them in the presence of a nickel catalyst?
questions.solution: **Hydrogenation** adds **hydrogen** to unsaturated vegetable oils in the presence of a nickel catalyst, which turns them into solid fat (vanaspati).
questions.shortcut: Vanaspati = hydrogenated oil.

questions.q: Night blindness is caused by a deficiency of which vitamin?
questions.solution: The eye needs **vitamin A** (retinol) to make the pigment rhodopsin, which is required for seeing in dim light. A shortage causes **night blindness**.
questions.shortcut: A for eyes: vitamin A → night blindness.

questions.q: Which blood components help in the clotting of blood?
questions.solution: **Platelets** (thrombocytes) gather at a wound and start the clotting process. Red blood cells carry oxygen, and white blood cells fight infection.
questions.shortcut: Platelets plug the leak.

questions.q: Which country hosted the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.solution: The first FIFA World Cup was held in **Uruguay** in 1930, and Uruguay also won it.
questions.shortcut: 1930: Uruguay hosted and won.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
questions.solution: The **WHO** is headquartered in **Geneva**, Switzerland. New York hosts the UN headquarters, Paris hosts UNESCO, and Vienna hosts the IAEA.
questions.shortcut: Geneva = WHO, ILO and WTO.

questions.q: Which Indian city was chosen to host the 2028 World Athletics Indoor Championships?
questions.solution: **Bhubaneswar** (Odisha) was chosen to host the **2028 World Athletics Indoor Championships** — a first for India at this event.
questions.shortcut: Odisha = athletics host state of choice (Reliance-supported centres, 2028 Indoors).
